title: Semantic fingerprint acceptance matrix and regression harness for batching/cache autotune
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Goal: build a robust, low-friction acceptance matrix that ties automated batching/cache recommendations to a deterministic quality fingerprint and a staged apply/rollback choreography. We want safe cost wins: when the cost autotuner suggests more aggressive batching or prefix caching profiles, the platform can run an automated verification suite that combines semantic fingerprints, distribution checks, and lightweight human audits to either approve, gate, or rollback the change. This ticket implements the acceptance matrix, the evaluation harness for synthetic/adversarial golden prompts, and the automated rollback triggers for canary/progressive rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic semantic fingerprint (SFS) is computed for a given model+config and a canonical prompt set; SFS delta threshold is documented and enforced
Automated generation of 3 adversarial prompt families per workload (short/long/context-shift) and inclusion in the acceptance suite
Canary pipeline: 5% traffic shadowed with new batching/cache profile; automated checks run in <30 minutes and return pass/fail
Auto-rollback triggers implemented: failing SFS thresholds OR token-KL > configured limit OR p95 latency regression > 10%
Human audit workflow: 50 sampled dialogs per failing canary with reviewer UI and note capture; audit must complete within 24 hours or pipeline rolls back automatically
Operational metrics surfaced in Console: per-candidate cost delta, SFS delta, embedding-sim mean, token-KL, p95 latency, and rollout percent
implementation_notes: Compute semantic fingerprint using ensemble of embedding models + PCA to produce a compact vector (256 dims) per canonical prompt and aggregate by workload
Use cosine similarity on the ensemble-averaged embedding to derive the SFS score; store baseline SFS per model-version in the config registry
Token-level distribution drift measured by KL divergence on model token probability distributions sampled via temperature=0.7 decoding over golden prompts
Integrate with existing canary runner (ENG-31209) to shadow requests and collect outputs into a temporary evaluation dataset
Add lightweight DB table for candidate runs: candidate_id, model_version, config_hash, start_ts, end_ts, metrics_blob (stringified JSON), verdict
Expose thresholds as config flags per customer tier and per project (defaults documented in AutoCost playbook)
playbook: 1) On config recommendation: generate candidate_id and snapshot baseline SFS, baseline metrics
2) Kick off canary: shadow 5% of production requests to candidate path for 30 minutes or 1k requests (whichever comes first)
3) Run evaluation harness: golden prompt families + adversarial variants + stratified production sample
4) Compute metrics and apply acceptance matrix rules (see metrics section)
5) If pass: promote candidate to progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows), else: mark failed and notify PM/ops
6) If failure during rollout: automatic rollback to prior config; create incident with run artifacts and open follow-up ENG ticket for root cause
7) For borderline failures: escalate to human audit where reviewers grade sampled outputs and can override automated verdict (override requires 2 reviewers)
metrics: Semantic Fingerprint Score (SFS): ensemble cosine similarity delta relative to baseline; pass if delta >= -0.08
Embedding mean similarity: pass if mean >= 0.91 on golden prompts
Token KL divergence: pass if KL <= 0.15
p95 latency regression: pass if p95 <= baseline * 1.10
Cost delta per 10k tokens: expected reduction >= 8% for recommended config
Human audit score: pass if >= 80% of sampled items flagged as acceptable
tests: Canonical golden prompt suite (200 prompts) covering core intents and syntax edge cases
Adversarial families generated by fuzzing and paraphrase models, grouped by attack vectors: truncation, context-shift, persona-violation
Functional smoke tests for API compatibility (status codes, streaming, function-calls) run in canary
Stability replay: deterministic replay of 50 representative production sessions to detect stateful regressions
Human-in-the-loop review UI for sampled failures with quick re-run and annotate features
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives due to noisy SFS on short prompts. Mitigation: stratified thresholds by prompt length and ensemble smoothing
Risk: adversarial prompts do not reflect real customer failures. Mitigation: seed adversarial generator with real postmortem examples and customer-reported issues
Risk: evaluation takes too long and delays rollouts. Mitigation: parallelized eval workers and early-exit fail-fast rules
Risk: human override bypasses safety. Mitigation: require two independent reviewers and log justification with immutable audit trail
qa_plan: Unit tests for SFS computation and threshold evaluation
Integration test that runs a full canary (shadow pipeline) against a synthetic lightweight model in CI nightly
Load test to ensure evaluation workers scale to 10k requests/hour without impacting production serving
End-to-end acceptance test: simulate recommended config, verify auto-rollback on injected regression
